egyptian_nephthys.name: Mourning as a kite at the bier
egyptian_nephthys.notes: With Isis she utters the funerary lamentations over the deceased, the two sisters figured as kites (birds of prey) at the head and foot of the bier.

sources.reference: Pyramid Texts (Utterances on the Two Sisters); Lamentations of Isis and Nephthys (P. Bremner-Rhind)

egyptian_nephthys.name: Guarding the Bennu and the Osirian relic
egyptian_nephthys.notes: As 'Lady of the Mansion' at Hwt-Sekhem (Diospolis Parva) she protects the local Osirian relic, the Bennu bird, and the manifestation Neferhotep.

sources.reference: Wilkinson, The Complete Gods and Goddesses of Ancient Egypt, s.v. Nephthys

egyptian_nun.name: Raising the solar barque from the abyss
egyptian_nun.notes: At each dawn and at the First Time, Nun lifts the sun-boat aloft out of the primeval waters with upraised arms (Book of Gates, 12th hour).

sources.reference: Book of Gates, 12th Hour

egyptian_ptah.name: Patron of the Opening of the Mouth rite
egyptian_ptah.notes: As craftsman-creator Ptah is the divine sculptor whose tools animate statues and mummies; his priests at Memphis performed the Opening of the Mouth.

sources.reference: Sandman Holmberg, The God Ptah

egyptian_set.name: Commanding storms, thunder and the desert wastes
egyptian_set.notes: Lord of the deshret (red land), Set rules the desert, sandstorms, thunder and foreign lands.

sources.reference: te Velde, Seth, God of Confusion

egyptian_shu.name: Separating Nut from Geb
egyptian_shu.notes: Shu stands upon Geb and lifts Nut, holding sky apart from earth and creating the air-space (the void) in which life exists.

sources.reference: Coffin Texts, Spells 75-83 (the Shu spells)

egyptian_shu.name: Bearing the light and the breath of life
egyptian_shu.notes: As the luminous air he conveys sunlight and the breath of life; later texts make him a solar 'Eye' figure who returns the Distant Goddess.

sources.reference: Wilkinson, The Complete Gods and Goddesses of Ancient Egypt, s.v. Shu

egyptian_tefnut.name: Generating moisture, dew and rain
egyptian_tefnut.notes: First-created with Shu, Tefnut personifies moisture, dew and corrosive damp; the pair are the first elemental couple of the Heliopolitan Ennead.

sources.reference: Pyramid Texts, Utterance 600 (Atum's creation of Shu and Tefnut)

egyptian_tefnut.name: The Distant Goddess / raging lioness Eye of Ra
egyptian_tefnut.notes: As leonine Eye of Ra she withdraws to Nubia in fury and must be pacified and brought home, a myth she shares with Hathor and Sekhmet.

sources.reference: The Myth of the Eye of the Sun (Leiden Demotic Papyrus I 384)

egyptian_sobek.name: Solar creator-power as Sobek-Ra
egyptian_sobek.notes: Syncretised with the sun as Sobek-Ra, he is hymned as a primeval creator who emerged from the waters of Nun.

sources.reference: Sobek hymns, Ramesseum/Faiyum papyri; Pyramid Texts (Sobek as son of Neith)

egyptian_serqet.name: Causing the throat to breathe
egyptian_serqet.notes: Her name means 'she who causes the throat to breathe' — she both inflicts and relieves the constriction of scorpion venom and snakebite.

sources.reference: Wilkinson, The Complete Gods and Goddesses of Ancient Egypt, s.v. Serqet/Selket

egyptian_osiris.name: Embodying the regeneration of grain
egyptian_osiris.notes: Identified with the annual sprouting of grain, embodied in the 'Osiris beds'/corn-mummies of the Khoiak rites; his green or black flesh signals fertility and renewal.

sources.reference: Festival of Khoiak texts (Dendera); Plutarch, De Iside et Osiride

egyptian_ra.name: Self-generation and creation of the Ennead
egyptian_ra.notes: As Atum-Ra he engenders himself on the primeval mound and brings forth Shu and Tefnut, originating the Heliopolitan Ennead.

sources.reference: Pyramid Texts, Utterance 600; Heliopolitan cosmogony

egyptian_ramesses_iii.name: Repelling the Sea Peoples by land and sea
egyptian_ramesses_iii.notes: In Year 8 he defeated the Sea Peoples at the Battle of Djahy and the Battle of the Delta, the latter the first recorded Egyptian naval battle, commemorated on the Medinet Habu reliefs.

sources.reference: Medinet Habu war reliefs and inscriptions; Great Harris Papyrus (P. Harris I)

egyptian_ramesses_iv.name: Marshalling the great Wadi Hammamat expedition
egyptian_ramesses_iv.notes: His Year 3 stela records an expedition of 8,368 men to the bekhen-stone quarries, the largest such enterprise attested for the period.

sources.reference: Great Rock Stela of Ramesses IV, Wadi Hammamat

egyptian_ramesses_iv.name: Exceptional temple-building piety toward the gods
egyptian_ramesses_iv.notes: His prayer-stela to Osiris/Amun begs long reign in exchange for unmatched devotion and monument-building, the program documented in the Great Harris Papyrus he completed for his father.

sources.reference: Abydos Stela of Ramesses IV; Great Harris Papyrus (P. Harris I)

egyptian_seti_ii.name: Reasserting kingship against the rival Amenmesse
egyptian_seti_ii.notes: After four years contesting the throne with the usurper Amenmesse he reasserted control over Thebes, erasing his rival's monuments.

sources.reference: Dodson, Poisoned Legacy: The Fall of the Nineteenth Dynasty

elamite_humban.name: Bestowing kitin, divine royal protection
elamite_humban.notes: Chief bestower of kitin, the protective divine authority that legitimises and safeguards kings, treaties and monuments; pre-eminent in the Neo-Elamite royal ideology.

sources.reference: Henkelman, in The Other Gods Who Are; Potts, The Archaeology of Elam

elamite_inshushinak.name: Tutelary lordship of the city of Susa
elamite_inshushinak.notes: Patron god of Susa whose very name (Sumerian nin-šušinak) means 'Lord of Susa'; protector of the lowland capital and its kings.

sources.reference: Susa royal inscriptions (Old and Middle Elamite)

elamite_napirisha.name: Sending forth the fresh life-giving waters
elamite_napirisha.notes: As 'Great God' of Anshan, akin to Enki/Ea, he commands the subterranean fresh waters, shown flowing from the disk-and-rod or from streams about his throne.

sources.reference: Potts, The Archaeology of Elam; Amiet, on the Susa serpent-throne seals

elamite_pinikir.name: Shining as the planet Venus
elamite_pinikir.notes: Astral goddess equated with Ninsianna and Ishtar as the Venus-star; sovereign of the sky.

sources.reference: Emar god-list (Pinikir = Ninsianna); Hurrian Goddess-of-the-Night ritual texts

elamite_nahhunte.name: Bringing forth life as the rising sun
elamite_nahhunte.notes: Solar god and 'bringer of life'; his logogram dUTU in Elamite legal texts marks him as the divine guarantor of law and contract.

sources.reference: Elamite legal and administrative texts (dUTH = Nahhunte); An = Anum (Divine Seven of Elam)

emotan.name: Sheltering the exiled prince Ogun (Ewuare)
emotan.notes: During the Uwaifiokun usurpation she sheltered and warned the exiled prince Ogun, materially aiding his recovery of the throne as Ewuare the Great.

egyptian_ptah.name: Platform throne and feathered back-pillar
egyptian_ptah.notes: Ptah stands on a maat-plinth, a feathered/djed back-pillar behind him.

sources.reference: Sandman Holmberg, The God Ptah

elamite_inshushinak.name: Rod-and-ring (measuring rod and coil)
elamite_inshushinak.notes: The judicial rod-and-ring held by the seated god identified at Susa, mark of his role as arbiter and judge.

sources.reference: Amiet, on the Susa cylinder seals; Potts, The Archaeology of Elam

elamite_napirisha.name: Streams of flowing water at the throne
elamite_napirisha.notes: Flowing water issuing from the god or his vessel, marking his lordship over the fresh waters.

sources.reference: Amiet, on the Susa serpent-throne seal; Potts, The Archaeology of Elam

egyptian_ramesses_iii.name: Mortuary temple of Medinet Habu
egyptian_ramesses_iii.notes: His great fortified mortuary temple at western Thebes, its walls carved with the Sea Peoples battle reliefs.

sources.reference: Medinet Habu temple and inscriptions

esigie.name: Commemorative cast-brass royal head (uhunmwun elao)
esigie.notes: Brass ancestral heads of the Oba lineage on which carved ivory tusks were set, focus of the ancestor altar.

egyptian_nephthys.name: Cult at the Mansion of the Sistrum, Hwt-Sekhem (Diospolis Parva)
egyptian_nephthys.notes: Chief cult of nome VII, where she protected the local Osirian relic, the Bennu and the god Neferhotep; widely invoked in funerary liturgy beside Isis.

sources.reference: Wilkinson, The Complete Gods and Goddesses of Ancient Egypt, s.v. Nephthys

egyptian_nut.name: Worship at Heliopolis and the House of Nut at Memphis
egyptian_nut.notes: Honoured at Heliopolis within the Ennead and as a healing goddess at the Memphite 'House of Nut'; her image was painted inside coffin lids and tomb ceilings.

sources.reference: Wilkinson, The Complete Gods and Goddesses of Ancient Egypt, s.v. Nut

egyptian_ptah.name: Memphite cult of Ptah and the Apis bull
egyptian_ptah.cadence: continuous, with Apis installations and burials
egyptian_ptah.notes: Great temple at Memphis (Hut-ka-Ptah, origin of the Greek name 'Egypt'); the living Apis bull was venerated as the herald/ba of Ptah, buried with elaborate rites in the Serapeum.

sources.reference: Sandman Holmberg, The God Ptah; Apis Serapeum stelae

egyptian_set.name: Cult of Set at Ombos (Nubt) and Avaris
egyptian_set.notes: Earliest cult at Ombos/Nubt (Naqada) in Upper Egypt; later a major cult of the Ramessides at Avaris/Pi-Ramesses. Red cattle and antelope were offered.

sources.reference: te Velde, Seth, God of Confusion

egyptian_sobek.name: Cult at Shedet (Crocodilopolis) and Kom Ombo with the sacred crocodile Petsuchos
egyptian_sobek.cadence: daily care of the living crocodile; pilgrimage
egyptian_sobek.notes: Living crocodile Petsuchos kept in the temple lake, adorned with gold and fed honey-cakes; sacred crocodiles were mummified in vast numbers. Kom Ombo housed the double shrine of Sobek and Horus.

sources.reference: Strabo, Geographica 17.1.38 (Petsuchos at Arsinoe); temple of Kom Ombo

egyptian_serqet.name: Funerary cult and protective magic; shrines at Per-Serqet and Pselkis
egyptian_serqet.notes: Invoked by the priest-magicians (kherep-Serqet) against venomous bites; she guards the canopic chest and the viscera-god Qebehsenuef, famously as the golden guardian of Tutankhamun's canopic shrine.

sources.reference: Wilkinson, The Complete Gods and Goddesses of Ancient Egypt, s.v. Serqet; Carter, tomb of Tutankhamun

egyptian_sekhmet.name: Festival of Drunkenness / pacification of Sekhmet
egyptian_sekhmet.cadence: annual (at the start of the year / month of Tybi)
egyptian_sekhmet.notes: Red-tinted beer drunk in great quantity, with music and dancing, to 'cool' (hesep) the raging goddess and re-enact the trick by which Ra halted her slaughter of mankind; centred on Memphis and Lower Egypt.

sources.reference: Book of the Heavenly Cow (Destruction of Mankind); Festival of Drunkenness records, Mut precinct (Betsy Bryan excavations)

egyptian_wadjet.name: Cult at Per-Wadjet (Buto) and the Festival of the uraeus
egyptian_wadjet.notes: Tutelary of Lower Egypt at Buto, paired with Nekhbet of Upper Egypt as the Two Ladies (nebty); her uraeus was set on the royal brow at coronation.

sources.reference: Wilkinson, The Complete Gods and Goddesses of Ancient Egypt, s.v. Wadjet

egyptian_osiris.name: Mysteries of Osiris at Abydos and the Khoiak festival
egyptian_osiris.notes: Dramatic re-enactment of the god's passion, death and triumph in procession to the 'tomb of Osiris' (tomb of Djer); culminates in the Raising of the Djed and the making of grain-filled 'Osiris beds' (corn-mummies).

sources.reference: Khoiak texts, temple of Dendera; Ikhernofret Stela (Middle Kingdom Abydos passion play)

elamite_inshushinak.name: Cult of Inshushinak at Susa and the high temple at Chogha Zanbil
elamite_inshushinak.notes: Principal god of Susa; the summit temple (siyan-kuk) of the Chogha Zanbil ziggurat was dedicated jointly to him and Napirisha by Untash-Napirisha.

sources.reference: Chogha Zanbil and Susa dedicatory inscriptions

elamite_napirisha.name: Cult of Napirisha at Anshan and Chogha Zanbil
elamite_napirisha.notes: Head of the Middle-Elamite triad, worshipped at Anshan and at the summit of the Chogha Zanbil ziggurat alongside Inshushinak.

sources.reference: Chogha Zanbil dedicatory inscriptions of Untash-Napirisha

elamite_kiririsha.name: Cult of Kiririsha at Liyan and Chogha Zanbil
elamite_kiririsha.notes: Tutelary 'mistress' of the coastal sanctuary of Liyan (Bushehr) and honoured in a temple at the base of the Chogha Zanbil ziggurat.

sources.reference: Liyan inscriptions; Chogha Zanbil dedications

emotan.name: Shrine of Emotan at the Oba Market (Aro Emotan)
emotan.cadence: continuous veneration; honoured in royal processions
emotan.notes: Buried at her market stall, her grave marked by a living Uruhe tree that remains her shrine; every new Oba and Igue-season procession pays homage at the site as the Edo conscience of justice.

sources.reference: Egharevba, A Short History of Benin; Aisien, The Benin City Pilgrimage Stations

attributes.name: Basket-on-house (nbt-ḥwt) hieroglyph headdress
attributes.notes: Wears the hieroglyphs of her name, a basket atop the plan of a house/enclosure, on her head.

sources.reference: Wilkinson, The Complete Gods and Goddesses of Ancient Egypt, s.v. Nephthys

attributes.name: Winged mourner at the bier
attributes.notes: Shown as a winged woman or as a kite at the foot of the bier, mirroring Isis at the head.

sources.reference: Funerary papyri and coffin scenes
Pyramid Texts; Lamentations of Isis and Nephthys

attributes.name: Naked star-spangled woman arched over the earth
attributes.notes: Body bent in an arch over the recumbent Geb, supported by Shu, her skin spangled with stars.

sources.reference: Greenfield Papyrus; royal tomb ceilings
Book of the Heavenly Cow
Wilkinson, The Complete Gods and Goddesses of Ancient Egypt, s.v. Nut
Wilkinson, The Complete Gods and Goddesses of Ancient Egypt, s.v. Nut

attributes.name: Bearded figure rising from water, arms raised to lift the solar barque
attributes.notes: Anthropomorphic, sometimes blue/green-skinned or frog-headed, lifting the sun-boat aloft out of the abyss.

sources.reference: Book of Gates, 12th Hour; Greenfield Papyrus
Hermopolitan Ogdoad iconography (frog-headed male deities)

attributes.name: Mummiform man with skullcap holding a was-djed-ankh staff
attributes.notes: Shaven head with close-fitting blue cap, straight false beard, tight wrappings, hands projecting to grasp a composite sceptre of was (power), djed (stability) and ankh (life).

sources.reference: Sandman Holmberg, The God Ptah
Apis Serapeum stelae; Sandman Holmberg, The God Ptah

attributes.name: The 'Set animal' head
attributes.notes: Curved down-turned snout, tall square-tipped ears, slender canine body and an erect forked/arrow-tipped tail; a creature not matched to any living species.

sources.reference: Predynastic to New Kingdom representations of Set

attributes.name: Red colouring
attributes.notes: Associated with the colour red, the desert and blood.

sources.reference: te Velde, Seth, God of Confusion
Set iconography passim
te Velde, Seth, God of Confusion

attributes.name: Ostrich-feather headdress
attributes.notes: Wears one or more ostrich feathers (the šw-feather, a pun on his name); often kneels with arms upraised supporting the sky.

sources.reference: Wilkinson, The Complete Gods and Goddesses of Ancient Egypt, s.v. Shu

sacredAnimals.name: Lion (with Tefnut, the twin lions Ruty)

attributes.notes: Woman with a lioness head crowned by the sun-disk and rearing cobra; can appear as a full lioness.

sources.reference: Wilkinson, The Complete Gods and Goddesses of Ancient Egypt, s.v. Tefnut
Leontopolis double-lion cult

attributes.name: Crocodile head with plumed horned sun-disk crown
attributes.notes: Crocodile-headed man (or full crocodile) wearing a crown of ram's horns, sun-disk, twin plumes and uraei.

sources.reference: Wilkinson, The Complete Gods and Goddesses of Ancient Egypt, s.v. Sobek
Sacred crocodiles of Shedet and Kom Ombo; Strabo 17.1.38

attributes.notes: Standing female hippopotamus with pendulous breasts and belly, leonine paws, and a crocodile's back and tail; resting a paw on the protective sa-sign.

Wilkinson, The Complete Gods and Goddesses of Ancient Egypt, s.v. Taweret

attributes.notes: Slender woman with a scorpion (tail and sting raised, or stylised) on her head, arms outstretched in protection.

attributes.notes: Woman with the head of a lioness crowned by the sun-disk and cobra, often holding ankh and papyrus sceptre; her many seated granite statues line Mut's precinct.

attributes.name: Green or black mummiform flesh
attributes.notes: Mummified king with green (vegetation) or black (fertile silt) skin, signifying regeneration.

attributes.name: Seated god grasping serpents, holding the rod-and-ring
attributes.notes: On Susa seals a seated deity (proposed to be Inshushinak) holds serpents in each hand and the judicial rod-and-ring, approached by worshippers.

attributes.name: Enthroned upon a human-headed serpent, with disk and rod
attributes.notes: On the famous Susa seal a great god sits on a coiled human-headed serpent, holding the disk-and-rod with streams of water about him.

sources.reference: Amiet, on the Susa serpent-throne seal; Potts, The Archaeology of Elam
Amiet; Potts, The Archaeology of Elam

attributes.name: Idia ivory pendant mask worn at the hip
attributes.notes: Wore carved ivory hip-pendant masks portraying his mother, the first Iyoba Idia, their crown rimmed with Portuguese heads and mudfish; emblem of the queen-mother office he created.

sources.reference: Ben-Amos, The Art of Benin; Metropolitan Museum, Queen Mother Pendant Mask (Iyoba)
